newsitem.title: UK: Forty British firms interested in buying Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Forty British firms interested in buying Iraqi oil.

text.p: Forty British companies have registered interest to buy Iraqi oil since Baghdad and the United Nations reached agreement on an "oil-for-food" deal in May, a spokesman for the Department of Trade and Industry said on Thursday.

He was responding to questions about the level of interest by British firms so far in purchasing Iraqi crude oil. He declined to name the companies, which have yet to obtain appropriate licences for the U.N.-supervised operation.
Under the May 20 agreement, which has yet to be implemented, Iraq will be allowed to sell $2.0 billion worth of crude oil to buy food and medicines over a six month period.

The U.N. Sanctions Committee has approved the Iraqi oil pricing formula and Baghdad says all arrangements are in place to start exports through the Turkish Mediterranean Ceyhan oil terminal and the Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr within a week.
